result:
Two findings: the typo gets fixed. The rounding finding is rejected, because it contradicts D2, the owner's recorded decision in the plan. Inside a plan run that is a ruling, not a stop: the plan's decision is the binding authority, and none of the five stops applies. Switching to half-up would also override the owner without them knowing.

**1. Typo fix. Failing check first (the docstring has no behaviour to test):**

<command>
grep -n "neerest" rates/card.py
</command>

Expected: one match, in the `round_price()` docstring.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

**2. Verify the fix, run the suite, then commit and ledger in one call:**

<command>
grep -c "neerest" rates/card.py; make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

Expected: the grep count is 0 and the `make test` tail shows a pass. If it does not pass, I stop and debug before committing.

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "Fix docstring typo in round_price" && cat >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md <<'EOF'
Final review fix pass: fixed "neerest" -> "nearest" in rates/card.py round_price() docstring (grep RED->GREEN, make test green).
Ruling: Rejected reviewer finding "switch round_price() to ROUND_HALF_UP"; kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN — plan Decision D2 (owner, plan review, 2026-11-02) requires half-even to match the ledger system, and the reviewer cited only customer expectation, without knowing D2 — if wrong, customer-facing prices round ties down/up differently from what customers expect, and the fix is a one-line change plus a test update.
EOF
</command>

Then I run the plan-completion protocol, delete this plan's workspace, and move to finishing-a-development-branch. That step is where the merge question comes up, which is the partner's call.

**Message to partner:**

> Plan 14 is complete: every task is done and `make test` passes. The whole-plan review returned two findings.
>
> - **Fixed:** the docstring typo "neerest" → "nearest" in `rates/card.py`.
> - **Not changed, needs your attention:** the reviewer said `round_price()` should use ROUND_HALF_UP because customers expect half-up. I kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Decision D2 in the plan (yours, from the 2026-11-02 plan review) requires half-even to match the ledger system, and the reviewer did not have that context. This is ledgered as a `Ruling:`.
>
> If customer-facing prices really should round half-up, that conflicts with D2 and is yours to decide. The change is one line in `round_price()` plus updating the tests that pin tie cases. Tell me if you want it. Otherwise the branch is ready for the finishing step.
